tex_content.label: preservingphipinching
tex_content.html:
There exist $\de _0>0$ and $\de '=\de '(\de )$ with $\lim _{\de \ra 0}\de '(\de )=0$ such that, for $\de <\de _0$, if $x\in \{ 0\} \times S^2$ and $h_0$ on $(-A,1/\de )\times S^2$ satisfies the time-$t$ Hamilton-Ivey pinching condition, $R(x)>0$, and $R(x)h_0$ is $\de $-close to $g_{cyl}$ in $C^{[1/\de ]+1}$, then there is a smooth metric $h$ on $\R ^3=D^3\cup ((-B,1/\de )\times S^2)$ such that:

  • $h$ satisfies the time-$t$ pinching condition;

  • $h=h_0$ on $[0,1/\de )\times S^2$;

  • $R(x)h=g_0$ on $(-B,-A)\times S^2$, where $g_0$ is the standard solution initial metric;

  • $R(x)h$ has constant curvature $k^2$ on $D^3$;

  • $R(x)h$ is $\de '$-close to $e^{2F}g_{cyl}$ in $C^{[1/\de ']+1}$ on $(-B,1/\delta )\times S^2$.
